ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L561-1 to L561-59 of the Code monétaire et financier (AML/CFT framework), notably L561-2-2 and L561-46 on beneficial ownership identification; Ordonnance n° 2016-1635 of 1 December 2016 and Décret n° 2017-1094 of 12 June 2017 establishing the beneficial-owner register (Déclaration de Bénéficiaires Effectifs) kept at each Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; mandatory suspicious-transaction reporting to TRACFIN under Article L561-15; ACPR guidance and Tracfin's national money-laundering risk assessments.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against EU Council Regulation 269/2014 (asset freeze), EU Regulation 833/2014 (sectoral measures), UN Security Council consolidated lists, French national freeze orders published by DG Trésor, and — as standard bank compliance for EUR/USD clearing — OFAC SDN and consolidated screening lists. PEP determination follows FATF 40 Recommendations; any anomaly triggers mandatory declaration to TRACFIN under Article L561-15 CMF. For this Low_Risk standard-tier wholesale activity, simplified due diligence under Article L561-9 CMF is available absent a PEP nexus, but full CDD remains the default.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr — sole legal e-filing portal for RCS registration, operated by INPI); prior-art searchable databases at data.inpi.fr and RCS extract service at infogreffe.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company denominations must be declared in Latin (Roman) script; under the Toubon Law (Loi n° 94-665 of 4 August 1994) the statutory name must have a French-language version or equivalent usable in all commercial documents, contracts, and stationery. Foreign words are permissible only with a sworn French translation recorded in the bylaws; the name must be distinguishable from existing RCS entries and prior trademark rights.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Two-step remedy. (1) Administrative: counsel amends the distinctive sign and refiles the name via Guichet Unique within the 30-day reservation window; alternatively a written request is addressed to the INPI Director for rescission of an incorrect availability determination. (2) Judicial: if the Greffe refuses RCS registration, a formal application to rectify may be filed with the Juge du Registre of the competent Tribunal de Commerce within 15 days of the refusal notification; ultimate recourse lies with the Cour d'appel. Where a conflict arises from a prior trademark, opposition may be filed before INPI within two months from publication of the conflicting application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only through a licensed domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) under Articles L123-11-2 and R123-11 et seq. of the Code de commerce. The domiciliation contract must provide genuine premises, mail reception, and forwarding functions. A pure letter-box arrangement without administrative substance may be challenged by the Public Prosecutor and can trigger tax re-domiciliation; a physical address is considered safer for an import/wholesale business with customs and VAT registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate. Estimated annual probability of unannounced inspection is 15–20% for new companies using shared domiciliation addresses, versus 3–5% for owner-occupied premises. INSEE and URSSAF site checks and DGFiP tax audits statistically target entities at domiciliation clusters; a stockless pass-through optical frames wholesale model ranks low-to-moderate in inspection priority.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and R.227-1 to R.227-2 governing the Société par Actions Simplifiée; Articles L.123-1 et seq. governing the Trade and Companies Register; Articles R.123-1 et seq. governing registration formalities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The INPI single business-formality portal, with registration adjudicated by the competent Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce) for the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of incorporation submitted through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, including the constitution filing for registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation; the balance must be paid within five years of registration. Contributions in kind must generally be fully contributed. Cash contributions are deposited into a restricted account with a bank, notary, or qualifying payment institution, which issues a certificate of deposit. The deposit is released after registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The shareholders resolve that the Company shall issue and the subscribers shall subscribe for the shares stated in the Articles of Association, with cash contributions deposited in accordance with applicable law. The registered office is adopted at [full address] and shall remain effective until amended in accordance with the Articles. [Name] is appointed President for an unlimited term, with authority to represent the Company within the limits of applicable law and the Articles. [Name] is appointed statutory auditor only if legally required or voluntarily designated. The President is authorized to complete all registration and publication formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders, assisted by French counsel or a notary where appropriate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine the corporate name, registered office, share capital, share classes, governance rules, corporate purpose, financial year, and term. Prepare the Articles of Association and shareholder subscription schedule. Execute the Articles electronically or in wet ink. Notarization is not generally required for ordinary cash incorporation, but documents signed abroad may require legalization or apostille and certified French translations where applicable.
required_dossiers: Shareholder identification and beneficial ownership information
President identification and declaration of non-conviction
Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistent corporate particulars, obtain missing signatures, replace unacceptable address evidence, and resubmit the complete execution package.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bank, notary, or qualifying payment institution authorized to receive capital deposits
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital-deposit account in the proposed company name. Transfer the subscribed cash capital and provide the executed Articles, shareholder details, draft registration particulars, and identification documents requested by the depositary. Obtain the certificate of deposit and retain the payment evidence for the INPI filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to AML or KYC queries, correct the depositor or company-name mismatch, and obtain a revised certificate of deposit before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A publication service authorized to publish legal notices in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an incorporation notice containing the company name, legal form, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, term, President details, and registration particulars required by the applicable notice rules. Review the proof of publication and ensure the notice matches the Articles exactly.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a correction or republication immediately if the notice contains a material error, and attach the corrected certificate to the registration filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the electronic filing, select creation of a commercial company, complete the SAS particulars, identify directors and beneficial owners, upload all supporting documents, sign electronically, and pay the applicable filing charges. Confirm that the principal activity is wholesale distribution of acetate eyeglass frames and that no regulated industrial activity is declared unless the operating model changes.
required_dossiers: President declaration of non-conviction and parentage
Translated and legalized documents, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the INPI dashboard, answer registry queries within the stated deadline, upload corrected documents, and submit an amended filing where requested. A refusal may be challenged or cured through the competent Commercial Court Registry procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain registration identifiers and release capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent Commercial Court Registry and Institut National de la Statistique et des Études Économiques
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the registration extract containing the SIREN, SIRET, and principal activity code, together with the RCS registration confirmation. Provide the registration evidence to the depositary and request release of the restricted capital account into the operating account. Verify the company name, address, President, activity, and beneficial-owner data.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract or equivalent registration confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction of registry data through the INPI or Commercial Court Registry, and provide corrected registration evidence to the bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activate corporate governance and post-incorporation compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company President, shareholders, tax administration, and applicable employment authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt and retain the first board or shareholder resolutions, maintain the share register and transfer records, establish accounting records, register for tax accounts, assess VAT and intra-EU VAT obligations, and implement beneficial-owner, AML, employment, workplace, and data-protection controls. A statutory auditor is required only if applicable legal thresholds or specified control relationships are met, or if voluntarily appointed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct missing filings, submit late declarations with applicable explanations, and regularize governance or tax records before commencing material operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to ordinary wholesale distribution of acetate eyeglass frames. The local municipality, prefecture, or relevant inspection authority may become competent if the company operates a warehouse, changes premises use, stores regulated substances, or undertakes manufacturing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific manufacturing or operating permit is ordinarily required for wholesale distribution of eyeglass frames. Standard commercial registration, premises compliance, product-safety, consumer, customs, and tax obligations remain applicable.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition, through the competent regional environmental authority (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from project-level EIA for ordinary office and warehouse wholesale activity, provided no listed industrial installation, significant construction project, hazardous-substance storage, or material environmental impact is involved.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No activity-specific wastewater or VOC thresholds normally arise from wholesale distribution without manufacturing or process emissions. Municipal wastewater, hazardous-waste, packaging-waste, storage, and waste-transfer rules apply. Any future industrial process or regulated storage must be screened under the environmental permitting regime for classified installations (ICPE), with applicable emission, discharge, waste, and monitoring limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No general pre-opening occupational clearance is required for a standard wholesale office or warehouse. Premises open to the public must comply with Établissement Recevant du Public fire-safety and accessibility rules. Warehouse premises must maintain suitable fire detection and extinguishing equipment, emergency exits, electrical and structural safety, and any required periodic inspections. The employer must prepare and update the Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels, provide occupational training and personal protective equipment where required, and comply with workplace health and safety rules.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: DGFiP (Direction Générale des Finances Publiques) - French tax administration; professional online portal: impots.gouv.fr (espace professionnel / Pro TVA); single company-registration one-stop-shop operated by INPI: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; customs and EORI authority: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) via douane.gouv.fr / import-export.gouv.fr, using the DELTA system for export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) File incorporation of the SAS through the Guichet unique (single business-creation portal) with the M0/standard forms; the dossier is routed electronically to the commercial registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce), INSEE, URSSAF and DGFiP. 2) The greffe delivers the Kbis extract evidencing legal existence. 3) INSEE assigns the SIREN (9-digit), SIRET (14-digit) and APE/NAF code (for this scope: 46.46Z - wholesale of pharmaceutical and medical goods, including ophthalmic goods). 4) DGFiP issues the French intra-community VAT number (n° TVA intracommunautaire, format FR-XX-123456789) upon completion of the VAT/IS registration data; for an export-oriented wholesale SAS, VAT identification is mandatory from the first taxable transaction even when turnover is below the franchise threshold. 5) Apply separately to the DGDDI for an EORI number (FR + SIREN), required to lodge customs export declarations; EORI issuance normally takes 2-10 working days. 6) No French fiscal representative is needed because the SAS is a locally established taxable person; a foreign non-established entity selling in France would require VAT registration and, where applicable, a fiscal representative under Article 289 A CGI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation | Territorial_Scope: a French SAS is by law subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) under Article 206(1) CGI and cannot elect pass-through treatment; US-style check-the-box does not exist. France applies the territoriality principle: profits from businesses carried on in France are taxable in France, while profits from foreign permanent establishments are exempt unless an approved worldwide/consolidated election applies. For eligible small companies, a reduced IS rate of 15% applies to the first EUR 42,500 of annual taxable profit, with the standard rate of 25% thereafter.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election and no elective hybrid-mismatch rule for an SAS under French law; ATAD hybrid mismatch rules (Article 212 bis CGI) apply mandatorily. Available statutory elections include: (i) French VAT grouping ('assujetti unique') under Article 256 C CGI for financially, economically and organisationally linked French entities; (ii) French fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) under Article 223A CGI, electable by a French head company (SAS qualifying) that holds at least 95% of French subsidiaries; (iii) election for 'bénéfice mondial' or 'bénéfice consolidé' (worldwide or consolidated IS base) subject to ministerial approval under Article 209 CGI; (iv) option between the simplified real regime ('régime réel simplifié') and normal real regime ('régime réel normal') for VAT/IS reporting; (v) the parent-subsidiary regime ('régime mère-fille', Articles 145 and 216 CGI) is electable for qualifying shareholdings to exempt 95% of dividends; (vi) for SNC partnerships, an option for IS taxation exists under Article 206(2) CGI but is not available for a SAS, which is mandatorily IS-taxable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), acting as the monetary authority and central administrator of the French balance-of-payments reporting regime; banking prudential supervision is exercised by the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution), with foreign-exchange policy coordination performed by the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) within the Ministry for the Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France applies unrestricted capital and current account convertibility as a core principle of EU law under Articles 63-65 TFEU on free movement of capital and payments. No exchange control authorisation is required for ordinary trade payments, export proceeds conversion, equity injections, shareholder loans, or profit repatriation. A French SAS may freely remit dividends abroad once the corporate decision is properly adopted and the distributable accounting result exists; withholding tax exposure is managed through the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU corporate shareholders and through applicable double tax treaties for non-EU shareholders. Restrictions exist only in narrowly defined public-policy areas: EU and national financial sanctions, asset freezes, anti-money-laundering reporting, and the obligation to channel cross-border transactions through authorised banking intermediaries. In practice, French banks execute foreign exchange freely at market rates without central bank authorisation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed repatriation timeline for export proceeds in France. Export receipts arising from the international wholesale of acetate eyeglass frames may be settled in EUR or any convertible currency and retained on the company's bank accounts. The only administrative duty is statistical balance-of-payments reporting: the servicing bank reports cross-border payment flows to the Banque de France, and a resident company must submit a direct declaration where a cross-border financial transaction reaches or exceeds EUR 750,000 or where the Banque de France designates the company as a direct declarant. All export receipts must remain traceable through underlying invoices, customs declarations, and SWIFT/SEPA payment evidence.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility, limited to routine treasury operations including SEPA/SWIFT payments, FX execution, and multi-currency account management. French or EEA-passported electronic money institutions (EMIs) are authorised under PSD2 and supervised by the ACPR; a licensed EMI may open remote accounts for a French SAS, hold client funds under safeguarding rules, and provide API-driven payables and receivables platforms. Legal constraints: an EMI may not grant credit, issue commercial letters of credit, provide import/export trade finance, or act as a depository for share capital escrow accounts. Safeguarding obligations restrict the deployment of client funds to a narrow range of low-risk liquid assets. Therefore, the EMI rail is viable only as a secondary operational account and cannot replace the Tier-1 bank relationship required for capital deposits, documentary credit, and full cross-border liquidity management.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French regulation permits fully remote onboarding when customer identification relies on an ACPR- and CNIL-compliant electronic identity verification process or eIDAS-qualified digital certificates under Article R.561-22 of the French Monetary and Financial Code. Tier-1 banks commonly accept remote opening for a French SAS where all beneficial owners are EU/EEA residents and the corporate file is complete. For non-EU resident directors or ultimate beneficial owners, compliance committees generally insist on an in-person video interview and may require a physical visit to the bank's French branch with original passports and apostilled corporate documents. The mandate is discretionary and bank-specific; a prudent blueprint assumes at least one structured video interview, and for non-EU UBOs a physical meeting of the President of the SAS with the relationship manager and compliance officer before external payment limits are activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial ownership chain with multiple holding vehicles or unverified ultimate beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO register extract from the French commercial registry; signed organisational chart of the SAS group; apostilled certificates of incorporation and good-standing certificates for each intermediate entity; passport copies of all natural-person UBOs; notarised board minutes authorising account opening and describing the financing structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds challenge with respect to the initial capital injection, share premium, or anticipated transaction turnover
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original six-to-twelve-month bank statements of contributing shareholders; audited or accountant-certified opening balance sheet and latest financial statements; executed share subscription deed and bank attestation of funds deposit; pipeline contracts, purchase orders and proforma invoices proving the commercial reality of the ophthalmic frames wholesale activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person or adverse media screening flags on directors or counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport or national identity document copies; written explanation letter describing business background; negative screening outputs from EU, UN and OFAC consolidated sanctions lists; PEP status declarations; references from professional advisers; evidence of residence and tax registration including French tax numbers, utility bills and business licences.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume international settlement flows against a thin equity base or abbreviated trading history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed supply and distribution agreements for acetate eyeglass frames; purchase orders and proformas; transport documents including bills of lading, airway bills and CMRs; customs declarations; bank reference letters from prior financial institutions; VAT registration confirmation and the full K-bis extract of the French SAS.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual use of third-party payers, assignment of proceeds, or non-contractual settlement instructions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Mandate file with specimen signatures of all authorised signatories; board minutes conferring signature authority and dual-approval thresholds; underlying contracts demonstrating the legitimate commercial linkage for third-party payments or receivables assignments; complete SWIFT/RMA correspondent details and proof of the registered office.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity contributions are transmitted by foreign shareholders to France through SWIFT MT103 international wires with an explicit purpose code identifying the remittance as an equity injection (ISO 20022 purpose EQUI or GFIN) or as a shareholder current account advance (ADVC or INTE). All injections are documented by board resolutions, subscription deeds, and the bank's certificate of funds deposit where capital is being constituted or increased for the SAS. For cash share capital, funds must first be directed to the blocked capital escrow account and are released to the free operational account only after the company is registered or the capital increase is legally completed. Any non-EU remittance must pass through the French banking intermediary, which applies sanctions and reputation risk filters, verifies the remitter and the underlying transaction, and files the balance-of-payments declaration with the Banque de France where thresholds are met. EUR funds are typically available on a T+0 or T+1 basis via SEPA/Target2, and USD or other currency wires on a T+1 or T+2 basis through the correspondent banking network.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements against suppliers of ophthalmic frames and accessories are executed through SWIFT MT103 international telex transfers for non-EU suppliers, SEPA Credit Transfers for EU/EEA suppliers, and SEPA Instant Credit Transfers for urgent euro disbursements. High-value or order-backed purchases are settled by commercial documentary letters of credit issued via SWIFT MT700 and amended by MT707, or by documentary collections under MT740/MT750 where the bank intermediates documents of title. Standby letters of credit and bank guarantees support advance payment obligations to Asian acetate frame manufacturers. The treasury function operates dual-approval payment workflows in the bank's e-banking portal, transmits structured remittance data referencing invoices, customs references and transport documents, and ensures clearing in EUR via Target2 or in major convertible currencies via the bank's correspondent network. Trade-related FX conversion is executed on the same banking day at current spot or forward rates, with automatic confirmation and full SWIFT-standard payment tagging.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX transactions (T+2 delivery in EUR, USD, RMB, JPY or other trade currencies)
Plain-vanilla FX forward contracts (fixed-date and flex-date) matched to documented trade payables and receivables
FX swaps (swap de change) for short-term treasury liquidity management
Vanilla FX options (call or put with up-front premium) hedging expected bid and tender exposures in the eyewear distribution business
Cross-currency swaps aligned with trade-related borrowing and the financing structure of the French SAS
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) used exclusively to hedge restricted or non-convertible emerging-market currencies where onshore forwards are unavailable
Embedded currency conversion instruments inside trade-finance facilities and documentary credit structures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and the competent commercial court registry through the INPI one-stop shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must generally be approved within six months after financial year-end and filed within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The commercial court may order filing under a daily penalty payment and impose a civil fine generally up to EUR 1,500, increased for repeat non-compliance. There is no automatic statutory strike-off solely for late filing; registry removal or judicial measures may follow formal notice and prolonged inactivity on a case-specific basis

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and applicable annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Directorate General of Public Finance (DGFiP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within three months after financial year-end, or by the second business day after 1 May for a financial year ending on 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest generally accrues at 0.20% per month and a penalty of 10% may apply for late filing or payment. Additional penalties may apply for insufficient or omitted tax declarations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' decision approving accounts and allocating profit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records; filing with the commercial court registry is required only where the decision or attached documents are subject to statutory filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within six months after the end of each financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene or document the approval may result in judicial injunctions, director or officer liability, and accounting-filing sanctions. No automatic annual strike-off applies solely because the shareholders' meeting is late

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner and corporate register update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI one-stop shop and the competent commercial court registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual confirmation is required where no information has changed. Changes to beneficial ownership or control information generally must be reported within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to declare or maintain accurate beneficial-owner information may result in judicial injunctions, criminal penalties for responsible persons, and restrictions or rejection of registry filings. No automatic annual strike-off applies solely because there is no annual confirmation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Directorate General of Public Finance (DGFiP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual payment generally due by 15 December; a recurring annual declaration is not normally required unless business premises, activity, or other taxable information changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest and applicable tax surcharges may apply, commonly including a 5% surcharge for late payment. Repeated non-payment may trigger enforced collection proceedings; no corporate strike-off is directly triggered

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SAS generally must appoint a statutory auditor when it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at year-end: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional mandatory appointment rules may apply to certain parent, subsidiary, or controlled-company structures and where required by applicable group thresholds
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) rules for statutory standalone accounts. IFRS is generally relevant for qualifying consolidated accounts, particularly for listed groups, and is not the default framework for ordinary SAS standalone statutory accounts

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a standalone annual beneficial-owner confirmation where ownership and control information remains unchanged. The SAS must maintain its share-transfer records, register of shareholders, beneficial-owner information, director information, and corporate decisions. Transfers or control changes must be documented promptly, and beneficial-owner changes generally must be filed within 30 days
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and corporate officers
Minute Book or electronic record of shareholder and management decisions
Beneficial Owner Register or equivalent beneficial-owner documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 300-1,800 per year for commercial domiciliation or registered-office services; France does not generally require a separate registered agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 3,000-12,000 per year for a small or medium-sized SAS requiring a statutory auditor; complex groups and regulated or consolidated engagements may exceed this range

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard corporate income tax rate for financial years ending on or after 31 December 2022); reduced rate of 15% applies to the first €42,500 of taxable profit for small enterprises meeting CGI Article 219 conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax reductions include: (i) Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to €100 million; (ii) Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20% of eligible innovation expenditure up to €400,000; (iii) patent box regime granting an effective 10% tax rate on net qualifying IP income; (iv) Young Innovative Company (JEI) total social tax relief and partial corporate tax exemption. No discretionary tax holidays exist; these are purely incentive-based deductions and credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form n°2065 (Cerfa n°15998) – 'Déclaration de résultats' with annexes n°2065-SD, 2052-SD to 2059-SD; e-filing through the EDI-TVA portal at impots.gouv.fr (dématérialisation obligatoire for corporate income taxpayers).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December: the return must be transmitted electronically no later than the second business day after 1 May. For other fiscal year-ends, filing must occur within three months after closing, extended to three months and fifteen days when using electronic filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SAS corporate identity, SIREN, registered office, principal wholesale activity (ISIC 4646), fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the French tax-agent reference if a non-resident tax representative is appointed; foreign shareholders are not listed in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book net profit or loss before tax as per French GAAP income statement (annex n°2054).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile French accounts with the group's IFRS reporting; confirm acquisition and resale of acetate eyeglass frames from/to related parties is booked at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 334 (Résultat fiscal avant imputation des déficits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjustments for non-deductible expenses, deductible charges, CIR deduction, and corrections under Articles 209 and 212 CGI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident wholesale supplier must not be treated as having a French permanent establishment solely due to storage or product inspection; confirm no PE threshold is crossed in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating losses carried forward and currently imputed to taxable profit under Article 209 CGI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carryforward is capped each year at €1 million plus 50% of the excess taxable income; non-resident shareholders cannot apply personal losses against French profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed at 25% on the taxable base, or at 15% on the first €42,500 when the small-enterprise eligibility conditions are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SAS is a wholly owned non-resident vehicle, the reduced 15% rate may be unavailable unless at least 75% of the capital is held by natural persons or eligible SME entities and turnover is below €10 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to submit the liasse fiscale on time triggers a penalty of 10% of the tax due (Article 1728 CGI), increased to 40% if the return is filed after a formal notice, and 80% for fraudulent intent. Monthly late-payment interest at 0.2% runs from the original due date. Omission of annex forms (2065-SD, 2052–2059-SD) may attract a fixed €150 per form. Non-payment of the tax balance due with the return adds a 5% surcharge plus continued interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% (Article 119-2 CGI). Reduced to 0% for qualifying EU parent companies under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive when a direct 5% capital stake is held continuously for at least two years. Treaty rates typically range from 5% to 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner must provide a French tax-residence certificate (Form n°5000/5001) to the SAS before the dividend is paid. The payer then applies the treaty rate at source; if the full 30% was withheld, the recipient may claim a refund from DGFiP within three years by filing Form n°5000/5001 with the competent tax centre. For EU parent exemption, the parent must furnish a Form n°5001 and, where necessary, a commitment to hold the 5% stake for the required two-year period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to non-residents: statutory withholding generally 0% for arm's-length commercial finance; however, payments to a non-cooperative state (ETNC) attract a 75% withholding rate. Royalties for patents or industrial property: statutory rate is 33½% under Article 182-1 CGI, reduced to 0% for qualifying associated EU companies under the EU Interest-Royalties Directive; DTA rates typically 0% to 10% for industrial royalties and 0% to 5% for copyrights.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €400 million: mandatory Local File and Master File preparation applies when the French entity or its foreign parent has annual revenue or total balance-sheet assets exceeding €400 million. If below this threshold, full documentation is not automatic, but DGFiP may still require basic transfer-pricing evidence under Article L 13 B LPF where cross-border related-party transactions are significant.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate sector-specific Economic Substance Regulations comparable to UAE; however, anti-abuse rules under Article 64 LPF (abus de droit) and the anti-artificial arrangement doctrine require genuine economic substance. An SAS registered in France but without local premises, employees, bank accounts headed in France, or real management and decision-making is vulnerable to redomiciliation at its place of effective management, denial of treaty benefits, CFC recharacterization, and application of the 80% abuse-of-law penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating French wholesale revenues from acetate eyeglass frames, issuing or using false invoices, maintaining undisclosed bank accounts abroad, or artificially eroding profit through sham royalty payments to shell entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 1741 CGI, fraud is punishable by up to 5 years' imprisonment and a fine of €500,000. When committed in an organized group or through offshore concealment, penalties increase to 7 years and €3,000,000. Tax penalties of 80% under Article 1729-1 CGI plus late-payment interest (0.2% per month) are also imposed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations may be jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax and penalties; criminal courts can order confiscation of assets, personal restitution, travel bans (interdiction de sortie du territoire), and imprisonment. The limited liability of the SAS is pierced where personal criminal intent or fraudulent manoeuvring is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of Law / Artificial Arrangement (Abus de Droit)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a shell intermediate in a tax-favoured jurisdiction with no economic substance, while the French SAS alone handles the wholesale distribution of eyewear frames; entering into back-to-back distribution contracts with a purported sole purpose of avoiding French corporate tax; failing to maintain transfer-pricing documentation for intra-group frame purchases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article L 64 LPF, DGFiP may ignore the artificial arrangement and apply an 80% abuse-of-law penalty, or a 40% bad-faith penalty, on the additional tax assessed. The issuer is also exposed to a formal judicial sanction publishing the decision and to possible criminal tax-fraud referral if concealment is proved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who designed or acquiesced to the artificial chain face personal liability for the 80% penalty, professional interdiction from managing a French company, and civil restitution. A travel ban may be imposed while the criminal inquiry is ongoing, and a conviction for fraud can result in up to 5 years' imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving wholesale proceeds in cash or through informal value-transfer systems, trading through front agents to hide beneficial owners, or channelling funds through a non-cooperative jurisdiction (ETNC) without declaration. Even a low-risk optician frames wholesaler is subject to AML due diligence under the French Monetary and Financial Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article L465-1 CMF, money laundering is punishable by 5 years' imprisonment and a €375,000 fine; aggravated circumstances (professional habit, organised gang) raise penalties to 10 years and €750,000. Administrative sanctions by ACPR or the relevant authority can reach €100 million or 10% of annual turnover, plus an order to cease the business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal conviction, confiscation of assets, prohibition from operating a commercial activity, and travel bans pending trial. The SAS's limited liability does not shield directors from criminal AML liability; each director can be separately prosecuted even when acting in the corporate name.
